tasks.title: Force-push rule reads git configuration values
tasks.summary: The force-push rule reads a command named in a git configuration value (-c, --config-env, GIT_CONFIG_*, GIT_PAGER, GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF, -O) the same way it reads the in-line form.
tasks.objective: Make `checkForcePush` in factory/orchestrator/src/policy.ts read a command line carried by a git configuration value the same way it reads that command line typed directly. Today an inline `alias.` definition is refused by `definesInlineGitAlias`; extend the same reading to every configuration value that git runs as a command: a `-c key=value` or `--config-env=key=VAR` on the git command, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` / `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>` / `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n>`, `GIT_PAGER`, `GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF`, and the `-O<cmd>` / `--open-files-in-pager=<cmd>` option of `git grep`. Each value is read whether it is set on the git command itself, in an earlier `export` or assignment segment of the same command line, or through `env`. A readable value is dequoted and checked by the same force-push checks a `sh -c` payload goes through; a value the rule cannot read statically is refused the way an unreadable inline alias is, whatever its key.
acceptance_criteria: Each of these is refused with the force-push violation: `git -c core.pager='git push --force origin main' log`; `git -c diff.external='git push -f origin main' diff`; `GIT_PAGER='git push -f origin main' git log`; `env GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF='git push --force origin main' git diff`; `export GIT_PAGER='git push -f origin main'; git log`; `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.pager GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0='git push -f origin main' git log`; `git grep -O'git push -f origin main' x`; `git grep --open-files-in-pager='git push --force origin main' x`.

A configuration value the rule cannot read statically is refused, whatever its key: `git -c core.pager="$P" log`, `git -c user.name="$NAME" commit -m y`, `export GIT_PAGER="$P"; git log`, `GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF=$(cat f) git diff`, a backtick value, and `git --config-env=core.pager=SOMEVAR log`.

Each of these is still allowed: `git -c color.ui=always log`, `git -c core.pager=cat log`, `GIT_PAGER=cat git log`, `env GIT_PAGER=less git log`, `git -c user.name=x commit -m y`, `git log --oneline`, `git grep -n foo`.

`GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` is read entry by entry, each entry by the same rule as a `-c key=value`, in both entry spellings git writes: the single-quoted `'key=value'` and the `'key'='value'` form that git 2.31 and later writes, with several entries in one value separated by spaces and the two spellings mixed. Each case is its own named test in policyGitConfig.test.ts: `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'core.pager=git push -f origin main'" git log` and `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'core.pager'='git push -f origin main'" git log` are each refused with the force-push violation; `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'color.ui=always'" git log` and `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'color.ui'='always'" git log` are each allowed; `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'color.ui'='always' 'core.pager=git push --force origin main'" git log`, a two-entry value in which only the second entry changes what git runs, is refused with the force-push violation; `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="$X" git log` is refused as unreadable.
Every existing test in factory/orchestrator/test/policy.test.ts and policyHookEntry.test.ts passes unchanged.
Each new branch of the rule is proven by mutation: the result names, per branch, the test that fails when that branch is disabled.

The rule reads every value of every carrier the objective names and needs no list of configuration keys: an unreadable value is refused whatever its key, and a readable value is judged on the command line it sets. So `git -c user.name=x commit -m y` is allowed and `git -c user.name="$NAME" commit -m y` is refused by the same reading, with no key named in the rule.

functional_clauses: Extend the per-segment force-push check so the value of every git configuration carrier named in the objective is dequoted and checked as a nested command line by the same checks a `sh -c` payload receives (including `isUnknownForcePushShape` and the `+refspec` check).

Assignments in an earlier top-level segment of the same command line (`export NAME=value`, `NAME=value;`) are carried forward to the later git segment; `env NAME=value git ...` and `NAME=value git ...` are read on the segment itself.

A value containing an unexpanded parameter, a command substitution or a backtick, on any configuration key, and any `--config-env` whose value comes from a named environment variable, makes the segment a violation, matching how `definesInlineGitAlias` treats an unreadable alias. The key does not change this: the rule holds no list of keys.
All new tests live in the new file factory/orchestrator/test/policyGitConfig.test.ts and drive `checkForcePush` (and the public policy entry the hook uses) with literal command strings.

tasks.title: Force-push rule reads xargs and shell pipes; history-rewrite rule reads per command
tasks.summary: git arguments supplied through xargs and git output piped into a shell are read like their in-line forms; a read-only git search naming a rewrite word is allowed on a protected branch.
tasks.objective: Two behaviours in factory/orchestrator/src/policy.ts. (1) The force-push rule reads a git command whose arguments come from xargs, and git output that a shell interpreter runs, the same way it reads the in-line form: `xargs git ...` with a subcommand that is missing, unreadable, or one of the force-gated subcommands is refused; git output piped into `sh`/`bash`/`zsh`/`dash`/`ksh` (directly, via `xargs` or via `env`), `eval "$(git ...)"` and `source <(git ...)` are refused. (2) The history-rewrite rule (`checkHistoryRewriteOnProtected`) reads each top-level command on its own and does not refuse a segment that `isReadOnlyGitCommand` accepts, so a read-only search such as `git grep rebase` on a protected branch is allowed while a real rewrite elsewhere on the line is still refused.
acceptance_criteria: Refused by the force-push rule: `echo --force | xargs git push origin main`; `printf 'push -f origin main' | xargs git`; `xargs -I{} git {} < cmds.txt`; `git log --format=%s | sh`; `git show HEAD:run.sh | bash`; `git log | xargs sh -c 'git push -f origin main'`; `git log | env bash`; `eval "$(git log -1 --format=%B)"`; `source <(git show HEAD:x.sh)`.

Allowed: `git ls-files | xargs grep x`; `git ls-files -z | xargs -0 git add`; `git diff --name-only | xargs git log --oneline --`; `git log | less`; `git diff | cat`; `git log | grep x`; `xargs echo < list.txt`.
With a protected branch checked out, these are allowed by the history-rewrite rule: `git grep rebase`; `git grep -n filter-branch -- docs/`; `git log --grep='commit --amend'`.

With a protected branch checked out, these are still refused: `git rebase -i HEAD~2`; `git commit --amend`; `git grep rebase && git rebase main`; `git grep rebase; git rebase main`; `git filter-repo --path x`.
A command line the segment splitter cannot read keeps today's whole-command reading for the history-rewrite rule (it errs toward refusal).

Every existing test in policy.test.ts, policyHookEntry.test.ts and task-1's policyGitConfig.test.ts passes unchanged; each new branch is proven by mutation and the result names the failing test per branch.

functional_clauses: In the force-push per-segment check, recognise `xargs` (with its own options, including `-I`, `-0`, `-n`) whose command is `git`, and refuse when the git subcommand is absent from the literal words, unreadable, or one of FORCE_GATE_SUBCOMMANDS; read-only and non-gated subcommands stay allowed.

Refuse a pipeline where a segment after a `|` whose earlier segment runs git is a shell interpreter (sh, bash, zsh, dash, ksh), directly or through `xargs` or `env`; also refuse `eval` of a command substitution that runs git and `source`/`.` of a process substitution that runs git.

Change `checkHistoryRewriteOnProtected` to evaluate the rewrite predicates per `topLevelCommands` segment and skip a segment `isReadOnlyGitCommand` accepts; when the splitter returns the whole line as one unreadable segment, keep today's whole-command match.

tasks.title: Trial recording harness: prepare, record, summarize
tasks.summary: A harness that prepares a trial workspace and prompt, records one run's check result, transcript tokens and diff as a JSONL line, and summarizes runs with NOT MEASURED for every missing value.
tasks.objective: Create the trial harness. Logic in factory/orchestrator/src/trial/harness.ts (tested under the root suite), a thin entry trial/harness/trial.mjs that imports the built module, and trial/README.md. Verbs: `prepare --task <kind> --arm plain|blacksmith --dir <empty dir>` copies trial/sample-app, applies the start state (the task's unified diff with `git apply` when the manifest names one, nothing when `start_state` is null), runs `git init` with one commit, and prints the prompt and the command the operator runs; it never launches claude. `record --task <kind> --arm <arm> --dir <dir> --cli-session <id> [--claude-config-dir] [--interventions <n>] --results <file.jsonl>` runs the hidden check, reads tokens through task-4's reader, computes diff stats against the start commit, and appends one record. `summarize --results <file>` prints a Markdown table per kind and arm with `NOT MEASURED` for every missing cell. A record has exactly: task_kind, arm, check (passed|failed|not-run|unknown), tokens ({used, complete} or null), wall_clock_ms (or null), diff {files, added, removed}, interventions (or null), cli_session_id, recorded_at, harness_version.
acceptance_criteria: Root-suite tests drive prepare, record and summarize against temp dirs and fixture transcripts; prepare never spawns claude (asserted by an injected spawner). A case gives `record` a fixture manifest whose `fail_to_pass` and `pass_to_pass` name non-default directories and asserts the harness runs the files in exactly those directories; one failing fail_to_pass file, or one failing pass_to_pass file, each stores `check: failed`.
A record with no transcript found stores tokens null and summarize prints NOT MEASURED; a check that could not run stores `not-run`, an errored check `unknown`; neither is ever `passed`.
summarize never computes a mean or a ratio from fewer than one recorded run per cell and labels every cell with its run count; with one run it says single run.
The record field set matches the plan's list exactly, pinned by a test.
trial/README.md explains the three verbs, says running the trial (and its spend) is the operator's decision, and contains no measured number.

wall_clock_ms is the span between the first and last timestamp of the run's main transcript when it is found, else null; interventions comes only from the operator's --interventions flag, else null. Neither is ever estimated.
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes: the doc guards walk every tracked Markdown file, so trial/README.md is held to them.

functional_clauses: Implement the three verbs in harness.ts with injected filesystem, clock, spawner and token reader; trial.mjs only parses argv and calls them.
Use task-4's transcript reader for tokens; do not re-implement token counting.

Read task manifests from trial/tasks/<kind>/manifest.json as written by task-9, and take the hidden check's two directories from the manifest's `fail_to_pass` and `pass_to_pass` fields, never from a hard-coded path. `record` runs each test file in both directories with `node --test <file>`, the prepared copy as working directory, and stores `check: passed` only when every file in both exits 0, `failed` when any exits non-zero, and `not-run` when a directory the manifest names is missing or holds no test file. tasks.title: Force-push rule reads git configuration values
tasks.summary: The force-push rule reads a command named in a git configuration value (-c, --config-env, GIT_CONFIG_*, GIT_PAGER, GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF, -O) the same way it reads the in-line form.
tasks.objective: Make `checkForcePush` in factory/orchestrator/src/policy.ts read a command line carried by a git configuration value the same way it reads that command line typed directly. Today an inline `alias.` definition is refused by `definesInlineGitAlias`; extend the same reading to every configuration value that git runs as a command: a `-c key=value` or `--config-env=key=VAR` on the git command, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` / `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>` / `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n>`, `GIT_PAGER`, `GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF`, and the `-O<cmd>` / `--open-files-in-pager=<cmd>` option of `git grep`. Each value is read whether it is set on the git command itself, in an earlier `export` or assignment segment of the same command line, or through `env`. A readable value is dequoted and checked by the same force-push checks a `sh -c` payload goes through; a value the rule cannot read statically is refused the way an unreadable inline alias is, whatever its key.
acceptance_criteria: Each of these is refused with the force-push violation: `git -c core.pager='git push --force origin main' log`; `git -c diff.external='git push -f origin main' diff`; `GIT_PAGER='git push -f origin main' git log`; `env GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF='git push --force origin main' git diff`; `export GIT_PAGER='git push -f origin main'; git log`; `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=core.pager GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0='git push -f origin main' git log`; `git grep -O'git push -f origin main' x`; `git grep --open-files-in-pager='git push --force origin main' x`.

A configuration value the rule cannot read statically is refused, whatever its key: `git -c core.pager="$P" log`, `git -c user.name="$NAME" commit -m y`, `export GIT_PAGER="$P"; git log`, `GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF=$(cat f) git diff`, a backtick value, and `git --config-env=core.pager=SOMEVAR log`.

Each of these is still allowed: `git -c color.ui=always log`, `git -c core.pager=cat log`, `GIT_PAGER=cat git log`, `env GIT_PAGER=less git log`, `git -c user.name=x commit -m y`, `git log --oneline`, `git grep -n foo`.

`GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` is read entry by entry, each entry by the same rule as a `-c key=value`, in both entry spellings git writes: the single-quoted `'key=value'` and the `'key'='value'` form that git 2.31 and later writes, with several entries in one value separated by spaces and the two spellings mixed. Each case is its own named test in policyGitConfig.test.ts: `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'core.pager=git push -f origin main'" git log` and `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'core.pager'='git push -f origin main'" git log` are each refused with the force-push violation; `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'color.ui=always'" git log` and `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'color.ui'='always'" git log` are each allowed; `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="'color.ui'='always' 'core.pager=git push --force origin main'" git log`, a two-entry value in which only the second entry changes what git runs, is refused with the force-push violation; `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS="$X" git log` is refused as unreadable.

Every existing test in factory/orchestrator/test/policy.test.ts and policyHookEntry.test.ts passes unchanged, with one named exception: the existing case `git --config-env=user.email=E push origin feat` in the policy.test.ts table titled 'allows %s — inline config that never names an alias' moves to a refused case, because criterion 2 refuses a `--config-env` value read from a named environment variable whatever its key. The two other cases of that table stay allowed, and no other line of policy.test.ts changes.
Each new branch of the rule is proven by mutation: the result names, per branch, the test that fails when that branch is disabled.

The rule reads every value of every carrier the objective names and needs no list of configuration keys: an unreadable value is refused whatever its key, and a readable value is judged on the command line it sets. So `git -c user.name=x commit -m y` is allowed and `git -c user.name="$NAME" commit -m y` is refused by the same reading, with no key named in the rule.

functional_clauses: Extend the per-segment force-push check so the value of every git configuration carrier named in the objective is dequoted and checked as a nested command line by the same checks a `sh -c` payload receives (including `isUnknownForcePushShape` and the `+refspec` check).

Assignments in an earlier top-level segment of the same command line (`export NAME=value`, `NAME=value;`) are carried forward to the later git segment; `env NAME=value git ...` and `NAME=value git ...` are read on the segment itself.

A value containing an unexpanded parameter, a command substitution or a backtick, on any configuration key, and any `--config-env` whose value comes from a named environment variable, makes the segment a violation, matching how `definesInlineGitAlias` treats an unreadable alias. The key does not change this: the rule holds no list of keys.
All new tests live in the new file factory/orchestrator/test/policyGitConfig.test.ts and drive `checkForcePush` (and the public policy entry the hook uses) with literal command strings.

In factory/orchestrator/test/policy.test.ts, move only the case `git --config-env=user.email=E push origin feat` out of the 'allows %s — inline config that never names an alias' table into a test that expects it refused (the unreadable-value refusal of criterion 2), and update that table's comment so it names `-c` and `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>` only. Change no other line of policy.test.ts.
